extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary/enforcement staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: describes suspension, reinstatement/probation rules, OED procedural steps for alleged violations during probation, publication and notice obligations, and legal authorities. Intended to govern discipline of registered patent practitioners after state disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the suspension of Thomas V. Malorzo (Respondent) is hereby ordered for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the specific regulation authorizing reciprocal discipline and the regulatory basis for the ethics violation. Use this citation and violation category when imposing reciprocal discipline based on a state suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40-day window)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1), the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State Bar of Texas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When initiating reciprocal discipline under §11.24, the OED must mail a Notice and Order and afford the respondent a 40‑day period to file a response asserting any statutory defenses listed in §11.24(d)(1). Document service (e.g., certified mail) and proof of delivery are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond — no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that: (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) suspension of Respondent is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent's failure to timely invoke the statutory defenses or otherwise respond may result in a determination that no genuine factual dispute exists and allow the Office to impose reciprocal discipline without further contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and scope of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent (a) be suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non‑patent law before the USPTO for four years effective the date of this Final Order and (b) has the right to request reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 after serving two years of his suspension, and upon reinstatement, Respondent will serve a two year period of probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies both total suspension length and the earliest date for reinstatement petitioning (after serving a minimum portion). Use §11.60 for reinstatement procedures. The Order distinguishes between full suspension term and the minimum served before seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement and probation practice permissions/conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a reinstatement, Respondent shall be permitted to practice trademark and other non‑patent law before the USPTO during the two year period of probation, provided that Respondent otherwise satisfies the conditions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a) and unless Respondent is suspended during his probation by order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what practice is permitted during probation and ties probationary practice to compliance with §11.14(a) (requirements for reinstatement/conditions). Probationary practice is conditional and may be curtailed by further suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED procedure upon suspected probation noncompliance — Order to Show Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the two‑year probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, the OED Director shall: (a) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not order that Respondent be immediately suspended for up to an additional two years for the alleged violations; (b) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record Respondent furnished to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); and (c) grant Respondent fifteen days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the threshold procedural steps for alleged probation violations: issuance of an Order to Show Cause, service to last address of record, and a 15‑day response period. Follow service rules in §11.11(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED referral to USPTO Director after inadequate response
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that, after the fifteen‑day period for response and consideration of the response, if any, received from Respondent, the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent ... failed to comply ... the OED Director shall: (a) deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response to the Order to Show Cause, and (iii) argument and evidence causing the OED Director to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply ... and (b) request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend Respondent for up to an additional two years for the violations set forth in the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the escalation process and required contents of the referral package to the USPTO Director and the specific remedial request (immediate additional suspension up to two years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette — Notice of Suspension content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette: NOTICE OF SUSPENSION ... [text describing respondent, registration number, summary of suspension, statutory/regulatory citations, reinstatement/probation terms, and factual bases].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should identify the practitioner, registration number, the nature and length of suspension, statutory/regulatory bases (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59), reinstatement/probation conditions, and a brief factual summary of the underlying state discipline. Use the provided template language as a model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to other disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public under §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires affirmative distribution of disciplinary notice and reasons to state disciplinary authorities, relevant courts, and the public as specified in §11.59. Ensure records and addresses for such notifications are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room located at: http://des.usp.gov/Foia'?OEDReadingRoom.jsp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary orders and related decisions must be made publicly accessible via the OED Reading Room (or successor public repository) to satisfy transparency and notice obligations.
